title: Autotune SafePatch: SLO-first batching + caching apply and automatic rollback
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Goal: Deliver an automated 'SafePatch' flow that can propose batching and KV-cache configuration changes, apply them incrementally to serving clusters, and automatically detect SLO regressions (latency p95/p99 and throughput) to trigger deterministic rollbacks. The flow must: 1) surface cost/latency trade-offs for proposed changes, 2) include an enforceable limiter layer that prevents aggressive config from breaching SLOs, 3) route traffic by SLO risk profile during rollouts, and 4) run statistical anomaly detection on both request-level metrics and output-quality signals so rollback is safe and explainable.

Scope: prototype controller + API + runtime integration. The controller will ingest candidate config deltas from Optimize (batch sizes, KV cache TTLs, prefix caching hints, continuous-batching thresholds), evaluate against historical latency/throughput distributions, propose a staged rollout plan (fractional canary steps and per-token/time budget), and then orchestrate application across worker pools. The runtime must accept 'limiter' tokens that enforce per-worker concurrency and per-sequence batching caps. For detection we will leverage existing tracing and the Console's route-level dashboards to compute realtime p95/p99, queue-time, evicted cache hits, and a lightweight A/B divergence detector for output token distributions. If any metric exceeds configured guardrail thresholds (absolute or drift from baseline), controller auto-triggers a rollback with a reason and postmortem stub.

Non-goals: full autosuggest tuning (we'll accept static suggestions for now), global ML-based optimizer pivoting (future), on-prem packaging in phase 1 (we'll validate on Dedicated and Hosted only).

Acceptance criteria: 1) Controller can take a proposed config and produce a cost/latency delta estimate with confidence intervals. 2) Can apply patch in staged canary with route-aware traffic steering. 3) Limiters can prevent per-worker bursts that violate latency SLOs. 4) Anomaly detector flags and initiates rollback within N seconds of breach (configurable). 5) Console shows rollout state, reason, and per-step metrics.

Design references and links: Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPT/Autotune+SafePatch (draft), Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4781, Dashboard mockup: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/4cY/autotune-rollouts (view-only).

Initial rollout plan: 1) Lab simulation run against trace-replay (2 weeks) 2) Canary on low-traffic customer tenant with synthetic load (3 days) 3) Gradual ramp with automatic guardrail enforcement and rollback (1 week) 4) Postmortem + runbook and GA.

Open questions: - What minimal set of runtime limiter primitives do we need vs. modifying scheduler? (pref: soft token bucket + per-seq hard cap) - How to quantify output-quality regressions for non-deterministic LLM outputs? (proposal: proxy with reference prompt set + embedding divergence). - How tight should canary step sizes be to balance cost savings vs rollback churn?
comments: 2026-03-02 Maya Chen: Kickoff meeting notes posted. Agreed to build controller as a standalone microservice that talks to the runtime via existing /admin/config API. Action: Liam to prototype limiter token API by next week.

2026-03-04 Liam O'Connor: Prototyped limiter header: X-Worker-Limiter: tokens=100,seq-cap=512,burst=20. Initial lab runs look promising; p95 increased ~3% for batch size +2. Pushed branch to GH PR #4781 for review.

2026-03-05 Priya Nair (SRE): Flag — scheduler currently enforces global concurrency; adding per-worker limiter may interact with autoscaler. Proposed to add a 'limiter-aware' pod annotation so autoscaler respects headroom. Filing follow-up ENG-42035.
2026-03-06 Design review (Alex Rivera): Console UX needs a clear 'rollback reason' UI and ability to annotate postmortem links. Design doc updated with mockups.

2026-03-08 QA: Began trace-replay tests with 4 representative workloads (chatty, short prompts, long-LLM, embedding-heavy). Noted anomaly detector false-positive on bursty embedding traffic — tuning threshold needed.

2026-03-09 Liam O'Connor: Implemented canary routing by 'risk label' — we tag routes with risk=low/medium/high based on historical latency variance. Canary will pick low-risk routes first. Adding smoke tests and canary abort on p99 > baseline*1.25.

2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Product review: aligned on rollback SLAs (auto-rollback within 5 minutes when p99 breach persists for 2 consecutive windows). Action items: finalize detector window size and add observability hooks for per-patch diff. Assigned ENG-42012 for runbooks and playbooks.
